raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
Serving a Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoint with `--ep-size` > 1 on the W4A16 path added in #41389 aborts the GPU with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016`. Under expert parallelism the standard dispatcher hands each rank `topk_ids` where experts owned by other ranks are `-1`, and `_apply_triton_w4a16` feeds those ids straight into `counts.scatter_add_(...)`, which writes out of bounds.

**Where it shows up**
Every GPU that takes the W4A16 path with EP > 1. It was reported on #41389 for both gfx1151 and gfx942, and reproduced here on gfx1151. The path was also enabled on every HIP GPU that is not gfx95x or gfx1250 (so gfx942/MI300X as well), although it was written and validated for gfx1151.

**How to fix**
Send `-1` ids to an extra bucket that sorts last, is left out of the ragged expert counts, and is zeroed before the top-k reduction, and enable the path only on gfx1151.

This PR also addresses the review comments on #41389 that were still open at merge time: log once when the W4A4 checkpoint runs as W4A16, register the opt-out env var in `environ.py`, and reject SwiGLU variants the path cannot compute (`gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_beta`, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `swiglu_limit`, e.g. gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4, MiniMax-M3), which previously passed the `activation == "silu"` check and produced silently wrong output.

## Modifications

All runtime changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py` and only take effect on gfx1151.

- Gate: `_use_triton_w4a16` is now `gfx1151 and SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` instead of "HIP and not gfx95x and not gfx1250". gfx942 and other AMD GPUs go back to the AITER path.
- EP fix in `_apply_triton_w4a16`: `-1` ids are mapped to bucket `num_experts`, `counts` gets one extra slot that is dropped before `make_ragged_tensor_metadata`, and the scattered rows of non-local slots are zeroed with `masked_fill` before the sum over `top_k`. Everything stays on device, so CUDA graph capture still works.
- Env var: `SGLANG_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16` becomes `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16 = EnvBool(True)` in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (AMD section), read via `envs.....get()`. The name gains the `ENABLE_` verb required by the env-var conventions; it was only on the #41389 branch, never in a release.
- `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` raises `NotImplementedError` listing the unsupported SwiGLU parameters instead of running plain SwiGLU.
- `logger.info_once` reports that the W4A4 MXFP4 checkpoint runs as W4A16 and how to disable it.
- New `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe_w4a16.py` (stdlib `unittest`, `register_amd_ci(est_time=40, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")`), entering through `create_moe_runner` / `process_weights_after_loading` / `apply_weights`:
  - `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path`, `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path`, `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` (gate, by reloading the module with a mocked `gcnArchName`)
  - `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` (ep=2 outputs summed over ranks equal the ep=1 output)
  - `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output`
  - `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected`

## Accuracy Tests

Setup for all tables: 1x gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, 96 GB VRAM carve-out), tp=1, `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, `--attention-backend triton --context-length 8192`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-gfx1151-20260923`. Before = #41389 as merged; After = this PR.

**EP crash (kernel level).** This GPU has a single device, so EP > 1 was exercised by calling `_process_weights_triton_w4a16` / `_apply_triton_w4a16` with the `topk_ids` the dispatcher produces under EP (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B MoE shapes: 256 experts, top-k 8, hidden 2048, intermediate 512; random MXFP4 weights).

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ep=1 | runs | runs |
| ep=2, rank 0 / rank 1 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION` (code 0x1016) | runs |
| ep=2 rank outputs summed vs ep=1 output, N = 1 / 7 / 16 / 128 / 512 tokens | n/a | rel. error 2.26e-3 to 2.36e-3 (bf16 rounding of each rank's output) |
| CUDA graph capture + replay with `-1` ids | n/a | bit-identical to eager |

**New unit tests** (6 tests, 3.6 s, 29 s wall including import, on gfx1151):

| Test | Before (#41389 code) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path` | pass | pass |
| `test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151` | FAIL | pass |
| `test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output` | GPU abort (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION`) | pass |
| `test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected` | FAIL (`NotImplementedError` not raised) | pass |

**GSM8K at ep=1** (regression check for the default path). sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 questions, thinking off (`enable_thinking=false`), `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `seed=0`, 16 concurrent requests.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K score | 63.0% | 60.0% |

The 3-point gap is sampling noise, not a numerical change: at ep=1 the MoE output of `_apply_triton_w4a16` is bit-identical before and after (`torch.equal` on N = 1 / 16 / 27 / 512 tokens, max abs diff 0), because every id is valid and the new ops are identities. The end-to-end runs differ only through temperature-1.0 sampling with nondeterministic batching (200 questions give a standard error of about 3.4 points). With thinking off the model answers with `\boxed{N}` and little or no reasoning, so this run checks before/after equivalence, not the model's best score. For reference, before with thinking on scored 82.0%, but 31% of answers were truncated by the 8192-token context.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, input 512 / output 256 tokens, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `num_prompts` = 10 x concurrency, `--seed 0`, one run per row.

| Concurrency | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Output throughput (tok/s) | 8.45 | 8.34 | -1.3% |
| 1 | Median TPOT (ms) | 117.00 | 117.98 | +0.8% |
| 1 | Median TTFT (ms) | 458.8 | 491.2 | +7.1% |
| 16 | Output throughput (tok/s) | 92.53 | 89.78 | -3.0% |
| 16 | Median TPOT (ms) | 154.05 | 156.35 | +1.5% |
| 16 | Median TTFT (ms) | 5117 | 5534 | +8.1% |

The fix adds a `torch.where`, one extra bucket, and a `masked_fill` over the scattered `num_tokens * top_k` rows to every MoE layer, and they also run at ep=1, where they are identities. The single run per row does not separate that cost from run-to-run noise.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the PR flow. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge.

nodes.body:
The EP fix looks good. One concern about the gate: the W4A16 path from #41389 also works on RDNA4 today, and this PR turns it off there.

Tested on gfx1201 (RDNA4, 32 GB). Setup:
- `rocm/pytorch` ROCm 7.2.3 / torch 2.10, **no aiter**;
- Triton and `triton_kernels` at the versions the upstream ROCm 7.2 image pins (`triton 3.7.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410`, `triton-kernels 1.0.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410`);
- current main plus #43679 (sgl-kernel build for gfx1201) and #47254 (Triton attention by default on RDNA);
- `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, `--context-length 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.92`, tp=1.

| | server | gsm8k (sgl-eval, 100 q, thinking off, T=0.7) | c1 / c8 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (W4A16 path via the current gate) | up in 95 s | 57% | 31.8 / 246.9 |
| this PR | **fails**: `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined` (falls back to the AITER path, and aiter isn't installed) | – | – |

The 57% is in line with your thinking-off numbers on gfx1151 (60-63%). Your unit test passes here (6 passed).

RDNA3/RDNA4 are in the same position as gfx1151: no FP4 hardware and no AITER FP4 MoE kernel. So restricting the path to gfx1151 drops them. Would you consider keying the gate on "consumer RDNA" instead of gfx1151 only? For example:
- gfx11xx plus gfx1200/gfx1201, but not gfx1250, which matches `gfx12` too;
- or the `is_rdna` platform flag that #47254 adds.

gfx942 would still go back to AITER as you intend.

Separately, when the AITER path is taken without aiter installed, failing with a clear "requires aiter" error would be easier to diagnose than the `NameError`.

@hubertlu-tw before this merges, please see the RDNA4 data in my comment above: on gfx1201 the W4A16 path serves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 today, and with this PR it fails at startup. If you'd rather keep this PR to gfx1151 and the EP fix, I can send a small follow-up that widens the gate to RDNA3/RDNA4, with numbers on both cards.
@vivienfanghuagood Thanks. I can't verify RDNA4 here, so I will open the follow-up you offered and hope you could helpverify it on your side. This PR stays with the gfx1151 gate and the EP fix.

@yichiche sounds good. Here is what I already verified, so your follow-up can start from it.

**Change I tested** (one commit on current main, [`8990c87`](https://github.com/vivienfanghuagood/sglang/commit/8990c879ab8c2d319e6984a8acc87bfbba3f0849); feel free to take it as-is):
- the gate becomes `gcnArchName.startswith(("gfx11", "gfx1200", "gfx1201"))`, i.e. RDNA3/3.5 and RDNA4, with gfx1250 excluded;
- the log line and the env-var comment now say "consumer RDNA";
- the gate test adds `gfx1250` (keeps AITER) and `gfx1100` / `gfx1151` / `gfx1201` (W4A16).

**Results.** `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, tp=1, `--context-length 8192`, no aiter. Triton 3.7.0 + triton-kernels 1.0.0 (the upstream ROCm 7.2 pins). sgl-eval gsm8k, 100 questions, thinking off, T=0.7.

| | gfx1201 (RDNA4) | gfx1100 (RDNA3, W7900-class) |
|---|---|---|
| main before #47408 | serves; 57%; 31.8 / 246.9 tok/s (c1 / c8) | serves; 55%; 17.0 / 192.4 tok/s |
| #47408 | `NameError: e8m0_shuffle` at startup | `NameError: e8m0_shuffle` at startup |
| #47408 + this change | serves; 61%; 31.1 / 237.6 tok/s | serves; 58%; 16.5 / 174.2 tok/s |
| unit test (#47408's file + new cases) | 7 passed | 7 passed, including the two EP cases |

Throughput rows are separate server processes, so differences of a few percent are within run-to-run noise. On gfx1100 the base needed our `fused_add_rms_norm` arity fix, because vLLM is installed in that environment; that's unrelated to this path. Happy to re-run on both cards once your PR is up.

Thank you for validating the fix. We can create a follow up PR to expand the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE path for other RDNA archs with your help.
cc: @yichiche

+"""Quark MXFP4 MoE W4A16 (triton_kernels) path on gfx1151.
+
+The path must only replace the AITER path on gfx1151; other AMD GPUs keep AITER.
+With EP > 1 the dispatcher maps experts owned by other ranks to -1; the W4A16
+path must drop those slots instead of indexing with -1 (a GPU memory fault).
+"""
+
+import importlib
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe import MoeRunnerConfig
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher import StandardDispatchOutput
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import StandardTopKOutput
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes import quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes.quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe import (
+    QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=40, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+try:
+    import triton_kernels  # noqa: F401
+
+    _has_triton_kernels = True
+except ImportError:
+    _has_triton_kernels = False
+
+NUM_EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTERMEDIATE, TOP_K = 8, 512, 256, 2
+EP_SIZE = 2
+LOCAL_EXPERTS = NUM_EXPERTS // EP_SIZE
+
+
+def _random_weights(seed: int) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+
+    def u8(shape, low=0, high=256):
+        return torch.randint(
+            low, high, shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=g
+        )
+
+    # Scales stay near e8m0 bias 127 so outputs remain finite.
+    return {
+        "w13_weight": u8((NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * INTERMEDIATE, HIDDEN // 2)),
+        "w2_weight": u8((NUM_EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTERMEDIATE // 2)),
+        "w13_weight_scale": u8((NUM_EXPERTS, 2 * INTERMEDIATE, HIDDEN // 32), 118, 124),
+        "w2_weight_scale": u8((NUM_EXPERTS, HIDDEN, INTERMEDIATE // 32), 118, 124),
+    }
+
+
+def _build_rank(weights, experts: slice, runner_config: MoeRunnerConfig):
+    scheme = QuarkW4A4MXFp4MoE(
+        weight_config={"qscheme": "per_group"},
+        input_config={"qscheme": "per_group", "is_dynamic": True},
+    )
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    for name, tensor in weights.items():
+        param = torch.nn.Parameter(tensor[experts].clone(), requires_grad=False)
+        layer.register_parameter(name, param)
+    scheme.create_moe_runner(layer, runner_config)
+    scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+    return scheme, layer
+
+
+def _run(scheme, layer, hidden_states, topk_weights, topk_ids):
+    dispatch_output = StandardDispatchOutput(
+        hidden_states=hidden_states,
+        hidden_states_scale=None,
+        topk_output=StandardTopKOutput(
+            topk_weights=topk_weights, topk_ids=topk_ids, router_logits=None
+        ),
+    )
+    return scheme.apply_weights(layer, dispatch_output).hidden_states
+
+
+def _to_rank_local(topk_ids: torch.Tensor, rank: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # Dispatcher contract under EP: local expert id, or -1 when another rank owns it.
+    local = topk_ids - rank * LOCAL_EXPERTS
+    owned = (local >= 0) & (local < LOCAL_EXPERTS)
+    return torch.where(owned, local, -1).to(torch.int32)
+
+
+def _w4a16_enabled_on(arch: str) -> bool:
+    props = SimpleNamespace(gcnArchName=arch)
+    with mock.patch("torch.cuda.get_device_properties", return_value=props):
+        return importlib.reload(quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe)._use_triton_w4a16
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_hip(), "needs a ROCm build")
+class TestQuarkMxfp4MoeW4A16Gate(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        # Re-import with the real device so later tests see the real gate.
+        self.addCleanup(importlib.reload, quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe)
+
+    def test_gfx942_keeps_the_aiter_path(self):
+        self.assertFalse(_w4a16_enabled_on("gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-"))
+
+    def test_gfx1151_uses_the_w4a16_path(self):
+        self.assertTrue(_w4a16_enabled_on("gfx1151"))
+
+    def test_env_switch_disables_the_w4a16_path_on_gfx1151(self):
+        with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16.override(False):
+            self.assertFalse(_w4a16_enabled_on("gfx1151"))
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    is_hip() and _has_triton_kernels, "needs a ROCm GPU and triton_kernels"
+)
+class TestQuarkMxfp4MoeW4A16ExpertParallel(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        patcher = mock.patch.object(quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe, "_use_triton_w4a16", True)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+        self.weights = _random_weights(seed=0)
+        self.runner_config = MoeRunnerConfig(activation="silu")
+
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1)
+        num_tokens = 33
+        self.hidden_states = (
+            torch.randn(
+                num_tokens, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=g
+            )
+            * 0.1
+        )
+        logits = torch.randn(num_tokens, NUM_EXPERTS, device="cuda", generator=g)
+        self.topk_weights, topk_ids = torch.topk(logits.softmax(-1), TOP_K, dim=-1)
+        self.topk_ids = topk_ids.to(torch.int32)
+
+    def test_ep_rank_outputs_sum_to_single_rank_output(self):
+        full = _build_rank(self.weights, slice(None), self.runner_config)
+        expected = _run(*full, self.hidden_states, self.topk_weights, self.topk_ids)
+
+        combined = torch.zeros_like(expected, dtype=torch.float32)
+        for rank in range(EP_SIZE):
+            experts = slice(rank * LOCAL_EXPERTS, (rank + 1) * LOCAL_EXPERTS)
+            scheme, layer = _build_rank(self.weights, experts, self.runner_config)
+            local_ids = _to_rank_local(self.topk_ids, rank)
+            self.assertTrue((local_ids < 0).any())
+            out = _run(scheme, layer, self.hidden_states, self.topk_weights, local_ids)
+            combined += out.float()
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(combined, expected.float(), rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+    def test_tokens_routed_only_to_other_ranks_produce_zero_output(self):
+        experts = slice(0, LOCAL_EXPERTS)
+        scheme, layer = _build_rank(self.weights, experts, self.runner_config)
+        all_remote = torch.full_like(self.topk_ids, -1)
+
+        out = _run(scheme, layer, self.hidden_states, self.topk_weights, all_remote)
+
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, self.hidden_states.shape)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, torch.zeros_like(out)))
+
+    def test_clamped_swiglu_config_is_rejected(self):
+        clamped = MoeRunnerConfig(activation="silu", gemm1_clamp_limit=7.0)
+
+        with self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError):
+            _build_rank(self.weights, slice(None), clamped)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
The EP fix looks good. One concern about the gate: the W4A16 path from #41389 also works on RDNA4 today, and this PR turns it off there.

Tested on gfx1201 (RDNA4, 32 GB). Setup:
- `rocm/pytorch` ROCm 7.2.3 / torch 2.10, **no aiter**;
- Triton and `triton_kernels` at the versions the upstream ROCm 7.2 image pins (`triton 3.7.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410`, `triton-kernels 1.0.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410`);
- current main plus #43679 (sgl-kernel build for gfx1201) and #47254 (Triton attention by default on RDNA);
- `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, `--context-length 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.92`, tp=1.

| | server | gsm8k (sgl-eval, 100 q, thinking off, T=0.7) | c1 / c8 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (W4A16 path via the current gate) | up in 95 s | 57% | 31.8 / 246.9 |
| this PR | **fails**: `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined` (falls back to the AITER path, and aiter isn't installed) | – | – |

The 57% is in line with your thinking-off numbers on gfx1151 (60-63%). Your unit test passes here (6 passed).

RDNA3/RDNA4 are in the same position as gfx1151: no FP4 hardware and no AITER FP4 MoE kernel. So restricting the path to gfx1151 drops them. Would you consider keying the gate on "consumer RDNA" instead of gfx1151 only? For example:
- gfx11xx plus gfx1200/gfx1201, but not gfx1250, which matches `gfx12` too;
- or the `is_rdna` platform flag that #47254 adds.

gfx942 would still go back to AITER as you intend.

Separately, when the AITER path is taken without aiter installed, failing with a clear "requires aiter" error would be easier to diagnose than the `NameError`.

@hubertlu-tw before this merges, please see the RDNA4 data in my comment above: on gfx1201 the W4A16 path serves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 today, and with this PR it fails at startup. If you'd rather keep this PR to gfx1151 and the EP fix, I can send a small follow-up that widens the gate to RDNA3/RDNA4, with numbers on both cards.
@vivienfanghuagood Thanks. I can't verify RDNA4 here, so I will open the follow-up you offered and hope you could helpverify it on your side. This PR stays with the gfx1151 gate and the EP fix.

@yichiche sounds good. Here is what I already verified, so your follow-up can start from it.

**Change I tested** (one commit on current main, [`8990c87`](https://github.com/vivienfanghuagood/sglang/commit/8990c879ab8c2d319e6984a8acc87bfbba3f0849); feel free to take it as-is):
- the gate becomes `gcnArchName.startswith(("gfx11", "gfx1200", "gfx1201"))`, i.e. RDNA3/3.5 and RDNA4, with gfx1250 excluded;
- the log line and the env-var comment now say "consumer RDNA";
- the gate test adds `gfx1250` (keeps AITER) and `gfx1100` / `gfx1151` / `gfx1201` (W4A16).

**Results.** `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`, tp=1, `--context-length 8192`, no aiter. Triton 3.7.0 + triton-kernels 1.0.0 (the upstream ROCm 7.2 pins). sgl-eval gsm8k, 100 questions, thinking off, T=0.7.

| | gfx1201 (RDNA4) | gfx1100 (RDNA3, W7900-class) |
|---|---|---|
| main before #47408 | serves; 57%; 31.8 / 246.9 tok/s (c1 / c8) | serves; 55%; 17.0 / 192.4 tok/s |
| #47408 | `NameError: e8m0_shuffle` at startup | `NameError: e8m0_shuffle` at startup |
| #47408 + this change | serves; 61%; 31.1 / 237.6 tok/s | serves; 58%; 16.5 / 174.2 tok/s |
| unit test (#47408's file + new cases) | 7 passed | 7 passed, including the two EP cases |

Throughput rows are separate server processes, so differences of a few percent are within run-to-run noise. On gfx1100 the base needed our `fused_add_rms_norm` arity fix, because vLLM is installed in that environment; that's unrelated to this path. Happy to re-run on both cards once your PR is up.

Thank you for validating the fix. We can create a follow up PR to expand the Quark MXFP4 W4A16 MoE path for other RDNA archs with your help.
cc: @yichiche
